fixture_name: Express-collector corridor planning study — Canada TAC planning (Toronto context, PD-licensed portal)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Decision-load from simultaneous transfer-permission and signage changes at three interchanges on a 420,000 AADT corridor is a genuine planning-stage safety mechanism aligned with CRSAG's network-wide collision-avoidance objective.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal 'collisions elsewhere along the route' claim is anchored by the verbatim EV-CA-003 quote, and the change-scope/AADT premises come from recorded corridor inputs, with the inference mechanism transparently labelled medium-confidence rather than invented.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern distinct from any compliance question, invoking the CRSAG audit-objective semantics for off-project-limit impacts appropriate to an Alberta Stage 1 planning RSA.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable—quarterly single-interchange sequencing plus before/after speed-differential monitoring—and viable given the detector-based volume data already assumed available.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are correctly identified as not applicable on a controlled-access express-collector mainline and the exclusion is explicitly acknowledged with road_users scoped to vehicle occupants.
